items.title: Let $\sim$ be an equivalence relation on $A$ with quotient map $\pi : A \to A/{\sim}$, and let $f : A \to B$. There is a function $g : A/{\sim} \to B$ with $g \circ \pi = f$ if and only if $a \sim a'$ implies $f(a) = f(a')$; and such a $g$ is then unique

findings.symptom: The definition leaves kappa, x, lambda>=kappa, j(ell), j(kappa), and Lambda=kappa as ordinary prose text in the rendered ItemBody, while the adjacent formal display uses typeset mathematical notation. The screenshot visibly prints “lambda>=kappa” and “Lambda=kappa” literally.
findings.suggested_repair: Typeset the set-theoretic variables and relation in math delimiters, e.g. $\kappa$, $x$, $\lambda\ge\kappa$, $j(\ell)$, $j(\kappa)$, and $\lambda=\kappa$, while preserving the prose.

findings.symptom: Facts & Assumptions and proof prose render “kappa” and “lambda>=kappa” as literal baseline text in the claims about fine measures, unlike the typeset variables in the Statement.
findings.suggested_repair: Typeset these variables and comparison, e.g. $\kappa$ and $\lambda\ge\kappa$.

diagram_review.existing_diagram_review: No TikZ/tikzcd source or rendered diagram occurs in the assigned items, so no existing diagram maps, labels, orientations, or mathematical correctness required checking.

high_likelihood_missing_diagram_candidat.rationale: This is the standard quotient factorization property: the equation g composed with pi equals f is the central assertion and the statement supplies all objects and arrows. A compact commutative triangle would make the factorization and uniqueness visually immediate.
high_likelihood_missing_diagram_candidat.concrete_maps_and_relations: Nodes A, A/~, and B; arrows pi:A→A/~, f:A→B, and g:A/~→B, with g∘pi=f. Label pi(a)=[a], and note g([a])=f(a) when f is constant on equivalence classes.
